title: Best Time to See Rhino and Tiger in Chitwan
meta_description: Best time to see rhino and tiger in Chitwan: month-by-month weather, grass-cutting season, monsoon closures, best hours of the day and tips to improve sightings.
summary: February to April is the best time to see both rhino and tiger in Chitwan: the tall grass has been cut, the forest is dry and animals gather at water. October to January is also good for rhinos, with cooler weather. Mid-June to mid-September is the worst, as monsoon floods close most of the park.

sections.heading: The quick answer
paras: If seeing a tiger matters most, go between February and May, take a full-day jeep safari and stay at least three nights. If rhinos are the priority, any month from October to May works, because Chitwan's 694 rhinos (2021 count) are seen on nearly every safari in the dry season. The reason is grass. Elephant grass in Chitwan grows taller than a jeep by the end of the monsoon, hiding everything. In January and February, local people are allowed into the park to cut grass for thatch, and the park burns some areas, opening up the views until new growth returns.

Heat sets the other limit. From late April, daytime temperatures pass 35 °C, and in May and early June they can reach 40 °C. Animals move only in the early morning and late afternoon, and so should you.

sections.heading: Chitwan month by month
paras: The table gives typical conditions in Sauraha at about 160 m. Temperatures are daytime highs and night-time lows; individual years vary.

sections.heading: Why February to April is best for tigers
paras: Chitwan's tiger population reached 128 in the 2022 survey, and sightings have become more common since. Even so, tigers are shy, mostly nocturnal and perfectly camouflaged in grass and forest. In the dry months three things change in your favour. First, cut and burned grassland exposes animals that would otherwise be invisible. Second, many seasonal pools dry up, so tigers and their prey concentrate along the Rapti, the Reu and the remaining lakes. Third, tigers cool off in water during the hottest part of the day, and are sometimes seen lying in shallow streams.

Full-day jeep drives that go west toward the Reu valley and into the Meghauli grasslands give the best odds. Walking safaris occasionally meet tigers, but most walkers see fresh pugmarks and scrapes instead. Guides listen for alarm calls from spotted deer and langurs, which often reveal a hunting tiger before you see it.

sections.heading: Rhinos through the year
paras: Rhinos are far easier. They graze grassland edges and wallow in oxbow lakes and the Rapti, and they are active for much of the day in cooler months. From October to May you will almost certainly see them from a jeep or canoe, and often from the Sauraha riverbank at dusk, when they cross to graze on the village side.

In October and November the grass is still tall after the monsoon, so rhinos may be close but partly hidden; canoe rides are good then because rhinos come to the river. From February the grass is short and you see whole animals in the open, including mothers with calves. During the monsoon, rhinos move to higher ground and into the buffer zone, and are sometimes seen in fields around Sauraha even when park tracks are closed.

sections.heading: Best time of day for sightings
paras: Animals in Chitwan follow the temperature. The first three hours after sunrise and the last two before sunset are the most productive. That is why our packages book morning jeep slots and early canoe rides, with rest at the resort in the middle of the day.
list: 6:30–10 am: best for tiger, sloth bear and active rhinos; mist in winter can delay the start
10 am–3 pm: quiet, hot from March; good for birds near water and resting crocodiles
3 pm–dusk: rhinos and deer come to water; good light for photographs
After dark: rhinos enter Sauraha village; stay on lit roads and never walk by the river

sections.heading: Monsoon visits: what to expect
paras: From mid-June to mid-September the Rapti floods, many park tracks close and the grass grows fast. Some lodges close or offer reduced programmes, and jeep drives are limited to the buffer zone and community forests. Humidity is high, leeches appear on trails, and roads from Kathmandu can be blocked by landslides.

There are upsides: the landscape is very green, prices fall, and rhinos are sometimes seen in the community forests and fields. Birding is good for resident species. But for a first visit with rhino and tiger as goals, wait for the dry season. Park closure dates depend on rainfall each year, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Tips to improve your chances
paras: Small decisions add up to better sightings. These are the ones we build into our safaris.
list: Stay three nights rather than two, and include one full-day jeep drive
Split your stay between Sauraha and Meghauli to cover different habitats
Book the first jeep departure of the day and sit on the outside seats
Wear dull colours, keep quiet and switch off phone sounds
Bring binoculars and scan grass edges and riverbanks, not just the track ahead
Ask your naturalist about recent sightings and choose routes accordingly

faqs.q: What is the best month to see tigers in Chitwan?
faqs.a: March and April are the best months for tigers, with February and May also good. The grass has been cut, water is scarce, and tigers concentrate near rivers and lakes. Full-day jeep drives into the western sector give the best chance. Sightings are never guaranteed, even in peak season.

faqs.q: What is the best month to see rhinos in Chitwan?
faqs.a: February to April, when grass is short and rhinos graze in the open. But rhinos are seen reliably from October to May; Chitwan held 694 of them at the 2021 count. Canoe rides in October and November are excellent for rhinos at the river's edge.

faqs.q: Can I visit Chitwan in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes, but with limits. From mid-June to mid-September many park tracks close, jeep drives are restricted to the buffer zone, and some lodges reduce services. Prices drop and the scenery is green. For good rhino and tiger viewing, the dry season is much better.

faqs.q: Is December a good time to visit Chitwan?
faqs.a: Yes, for rhinos and pleasant days. Mornings are cold, around 7–8 °C, and often foggy until mid-morning, so safaris start a little later. Grass is still fairly tall, so tiger sightings are less frequent than in spring. Late December also brings the Elephant Festival in Sauraha.

faqs.q: How hot is Chitwan in April and May?
faqs.a: Very hot. Daytime highs reach 35 °C in April and 36–40 °C in May, with high humidity before the monsoon. Activities run early morning and late afternoon, with rest in air-conditioned rooms or the pool at midday. Carry water and wear a hat on safaris.

faqs.q: When does Chitwan's grass-cutting season happen?
faqs.a: Usually in January and early February, when local communities are allowed into the park for a short period to cut grass for thatch and fodder. Burning of some grassland follows. The cut areas give excellent visibility for several weeks afterwards, which is why February to April is peak viewing season.

faqs.q: What time of day is best for a jeep safari in Chitwan?
faqs.a: Early morning, starting around 6:30–7 am, is best for active animals and soft light. Late afternoon until dusk is second best, as animals come to water. Midday is quiet, especially from March, when heat drives wildlife into shade.

faqs.q: Are tiger sightings in Chitwan increasing?
faqs.a: Yes. Chitwan's tiger population rose to 128 in the 2022 survey, and naturalists report more frequent sightings, including during the day near rivers. Still, most visitors on a two-night trip do not see one. Longer stays and full-day drives improve the odds.

faqs.q: Is October a good time for Chitwan?
faqs.a: October is pleasant, green and clear after the monsoon, with festivals such as Dashain. Rhinos are seen regularly, especially from canoes. Grass is still tall, so tiger and sloth bear sightings are less likely than in spring. It is also a busy month, so book early.
